description: This study by Daniel Nguyen, Jonathan Levy, Jonathan Peters and co-authors (Journal of Exposure Science and Environmental Epidemiology, 2023) gives a national assessment of how aircraft noise exposure changed over time and across racial and ethnic groups in the United States. Coverage: noise contours for 90 US airports modelled every five years from 1995 to 2015 with the Federal Aviation Administration's Aviation Environmental Design Tool, for day-night average sound levels of 45 and 65 dB(A) and a night level of 45 dB(A), overlaid on census tract data from the Census Bureau and American Community Surveys for 2000 to 2015. Mean exposed areas peaked in 2000, fell by 37% between 2005 and 2010 and rose again in 2015; group-based trajectory modelling found four groups of airports linked to size and activity. Hispanic or Latino, Black and Asian populations had higher proportions exposed relative to their numbers than non-Hispanic White populations in all years. Format and access: an open access article. Licence and cost: free under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: modelled contours, not measurements, and tract-level overlay. The exposure method can be used to add equity weights to noise impacts in airport capacity and flight path scenarios. It relates to AEDT and the BTS National Transportation Noise Map in the catalogue.
